title: project-context
summary: Writes or checks the `.dlcontext.json` file beside a project: platform, config and define set, with the .dproj SHA-1 for staleness
intro: Read this when the language server or a tool must know which platform and configuration a project is built for without guessing. project-context resolves the .dproj (or, for a .dpr with no .dproj, the platform and config you pass) and writes the context file next to the project. --check writes nothing and exits 1 with the reason when the file is missing or stale. With explicit --db and no listed library for the platform, the server falls back to the central-defaults library.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint project-context --project <x.dproj|x.dpr> [--platform P] [--config C] [--output <file>] [--json] [--check] (writes <base>.dlcontext.json beside the project: platform, config and the complete effective define set, plus the .dproj SHA-1 for staleness; --check writes nothing and exits 1 saying why when the file is missing or stale; a .dpr with no .dproj exits 2 unless --platform and --config are both given)
help: drag-lint project-context --project <x.dproj|x.dpr> [--platform P] [--config C] [--output <file>] [--json] [--check] (writes <base>.dlcontext.json beside the project: platform, config and the complete effective define set, plus the .dproj SHA-1 for staleness; --check writes nothing and exits 1 saying why when the file is missing or stale; a .dpr with no .dproj exits 2 unless --platform and --config are both given)
see wiki page: project-context
drag-lint query --concept "<words>" [--place library,project,repository] [--links N] [--limit N] [--kind k,...] [--json] --db <db>
^ the repository is searched through the copy made by index --project; a changed repository file prints a stale note until the next index run.
^ by name only = a FieldByName literal whose dataset has no known table; it is listed under every table that has a field of that name and never raises a rank.
^ the library place is the resolved database named library-*.sqlite; --place project,repository skips it.
^ no stemming in captions: name does not find names.

^ a directory-scan index (`index <dir>`) has no project file and no repository copy: query --concept says "repository: not copied (this index was made by a directory scan and has no project file)" and places[].state stays not-copied-yet; run `index --project <X.dproj>`.

^ `place=

` is appended to a symbol or find-unit line, so a consumer that anchors on the end of the line (the [impl-only] or forward-at-line suffix) must allow it.
see wiki page: caption-concepts
drag-lint query --name <symbol-name> [--db ...] [--json] [--case-sensitive] [--exact] [--project <x.dproj> [--no-create]]
^ a project DB IS the compile closure, so a hit is membership and a MISS is non-membership.

^ STRING LITERALS, DFM, SQL *and COMMENT PROSE* -- // { } (* *) and ///. Filter with --kind: literal|const|resourcestring|format|comment|doc|dfm-prop|sql-exception. --kind literal is what this returned before comments were indexed.
see wiki page: query-name-like
drag-lint query --text "<phrase>" --near <QName> [--hops 1..3] [--hops-uses] [--near-boost] [--db ...] [--json]
^ The default RESTRICTS: a hit outside N hops is dropped, not demoted; --near-boost keeps it.
^ A hop is one resolved call edge, callers and callees; --hops 4 is refused (use impact --depth).
see wiki page: query-text-near

drag-lint rules disable|enable --rule <id> --scope line|unit|project [--in <F> --line <N>] --reason "<text>" [--project <.dproj>] [--config <drag-lint-lint.json>] [--json|--format json]   (line = a dl:ok marker on the line; unit / project = rule_overrides in the project lint config, with reason and date; enable undoes one disable)
